-- SQL-10: Cohort Retention
-- Tables: users(user_id, signup_ts), events(user_id, event_ts)
--
-- cohort_week   Monday of the signup date's week (ISO week start), as a DATE
-- week_number   elapsed weeks since signup, by calendar date:
--               (event date - signup date) in days, integer-divided by 7. Signup day and the
--               next 6 days are week 0. Events before signup, or after week 8, are ignored.
-- Only events from users in `users` count.
--
-- Create cohort_retention(cohort_week, week_number, cohort_users, retained_users, retention_rate)
-- with exactly one row for every cohort and every week_number 0..8, even when no one returned.
--   cohort_users    users who signed up in the cohort week (all of them)
--   retained_users  cohort users with at least one event in that week_number
--   retention_rate  retained_users / cohort_users
CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW cohort_retention AS
SELECT NULL::DATE AS cohort_week, NULL::INTEGER AS week_number, NULL::BIGINT AS cohort_users,
       NULL::BIGINT AS retained_users, NULL::DOUBLE AS retention_rate
WHERE FALSE; -- TODO

-- SQL-11: Experiment Metrics + Sample-Ratio Checks
-- Tables: assignments(user_id, variant, assigned_ts)   may repeat rows; a few users have two variants
--         exposures(user_id, exposure_ts)              many rows per user
--         conversions(order_id, user_id, conversion_ts)
--         revenue(order_id, amount)                    amount may be NULL (treat as 0)
--
-- Analysis population: users assigned to exactly one distinct variant ("clean" users).
-- A clean user's assignment time is their earliest assigned_ts.
--   exposed     the user has at least one exposure at or after their assignment time;
--               their first such exposure is their exposure time
--   converter   an exposed user with at least one conversion at or after their exposure time
--   revenue     amounts of those qualifying conversions only
--
-- 1. experiment_metrics(variant, assigned_users, exposed_users, converters, conversion_rate,
--                       revenue_per_user, assignment_share)
--    conversion_rate = converters / exposed_users; revenue_per_user = revenue / exposed_users;
--    assignment_share = assigned_users / all clean users.
-- 2. assignment_issues(user_id, issue), one row per user per issue (all assignment rows, not just
--    clean users):
--      'duplicate_assignment'       the same (user_id, variant) appears more than once
--      'multiple_variants'          the user is assigned to more than one distinct variant
--      'exposure_after_conversion'  the user's earliest exposure is later than their earliest conversion
-- 3. srm_inputs(variant, observed_users, expected_users, chi_square_component) for an intended
--    50/50 split over clean users: expected_users = 0.5 * clean users,
--    chi_square_component = (observed - expected)^2 / expected.
CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW experiment_metrics AS
SELECT NULL::VARCHAR AS variant, NULL::BIGINT AS assigned_users, NULL::BIGINT AS exposed_users,
       NULL::BIGINT AS converters, NULL::DOUBLE AS conversion_rate, NULL::DOUBLE AS revenue_per_user,
       NULL::DOUBLE AS assignment_share
WHERE FALSE; -- TODO

CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW assignment_issues AS
SELECT NULL::INTEGER AS user_id, NULL::VARCHAR AS issue WHERE FALSE; -- TODO

CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW srm_inputs AS
SELECT NULL::VARCHAR AS variant, NULL::BIGINT AS observed_users, NULL::DOUBLE AS expected_users,
       NULL::DOUBLE AS chi_square_component
WHERE FALSE; -- TODO

-- SQL-12: Point-in-Time Features in SQL
-- Tables: labels(label_id, entity_id, label_ts)
--         events(event_id, entity_id, event_ts, amount)    amount may be NULL
--         profiles(profile_id, entity_id, profile_ts, tier) history of profile values
--
-- Only information strictly before label_ts may be used (event_ts < label_ts,
-- profile_ts < label_ts). An N-day window covers label_ts - N days <= event_ts < label_ts.
--
-- Create point_in_time_features with exactly one row per label row:
--   label_id, entity_id, label_ts,
--   event_count_1d, event_count_7d, event_count_30d   events in each window (0 if none)
--   amount_30d     SUM(amount) over the 30-day window, ignoring NULL amounts; 0.0 if none
--   latest_tier    tier of the latest profile row before label_ts (ties on profile_ts go to
--                  the larger profile_id); NULL if there is none
CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW point_in_time_features AS
SELECT NULL::INTEGER AS label_id, NULL::INTEGER AS entity_id, NULL::TIMESTAMP AS label_ts,
       NULL::BIGINT AS event_count_1d, NULL::BIGINT AS event_count_7d, NULL::BIGINT AS event_count_30d,
       NULL::DOUBLE AS amount_30d, NULL::VARCHAR AS latest_tier
WHERE FALSE; -- TODO

-- SQL-13: Data Reconciliation / Quality Invariants
-- Tables: raw_events(event_id, source, event_ts, user_id, amount)
--         features(event_id, source, event_date, user_id, amount, feature_ts)  should hold exactly
--                  one row per raw event, with event_date = the raw event's date
--         predictions(prediction_id, event_id, source, prediction_ts, score)
-- Keys and amounts can be NULL. Amount sums ignore NULLs and are 0.0 for an empty side.
--
-- 1. reconciliation_by_day_source(event_date, source, raw_rows, feature_rows, raw_amount,
--      feature_amount, row_diff, amount_diff, status)
--    Raw rows are dated by CAST(event_ts AS DATE); feature rows by event_date. One row per
--    (event_date, source) present on either side. row_diff = feature_rows - raw_rows,
--    amount_diff = feature_amount - raw_amount. status = 'ok' when row_diff = 0 and
--    |amount_diff| <= 0.5, otherwise 'mismatch'. Row counts include rows with NULL keys.
-- 2. data_quality_issues(check_name, table_name, record_id, event_date, source), one row per
--    failing record per check. record_id is event_id (raw_events, features) or prediction_id
--    (predictions); event_date is the row's own date (raw: event_ts date, features: event_date,
--    predictions: prediction_ts date). Rows with a NULL event_id are only reported as null_key.
--      null_key                  raw_events or features row with NULL event_id
--      missing_feature           raw event with no feature row             (table raw_events)
--      unexpected_feature        feature row with no raw event             (table features)
--      duplicate_feature_key     event_id with more than one feature row; one row per key
--                                (event_date/source from any of its rows)  (table features)
--      feature_date_mismatch     feature event_date differs from the raw event's date
--      feature_before_event      feature_ts earlier than the raw event_ts
--      orphan_prediction         prediction whose event_id has no feature row, including NULL
--      prediction_before_feature prediction_ts earlier than the event's earliest feature_ts
-- 3. failure_summary(event_date, source, check_name, failures): issue counts per day/source/check.
CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW reconciliation_by_day_source AS
SELECT NULL::DATE AS event_date, NULL::VARCHAR AS source, NULL::BIGINT AS raw_rows, NULL::BIGINT AS feature_rows,
       NULL::DOUBLE AS raw_amount, NULL::DOUBLE AS feature_amount, NULL::BIGINT AS row_diff,
       NULL::DOUBLE AS amount_diff, NULL::VARCHAR AS status
WHERE FALSE; -- TODO

CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW data_quality_issues AS
SELECT NULL::VARCHAR AS check_name, NULL::VARCHAR AS table_name, NULL::INTEGER AS record_id,
       NULL::DATE AS event_date, NULL::VARCHAR AS source
WHERE FALSE; -- TODO

CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW failure_summary AS
SELECT NULL::DATE AS event_date, NULL::VARCHAR AS source, NULL::VARCHAR AS check_name, NULL::BIGINT AS failures
WHERE FALSE; -- TODO

import numpy as np


def pairwise_sq_distances(queries: np.ndarray, candidates: np.ndarray) -> np.ndarray:
    """Squared Euclidean distances `(m, n)` via the norm expansion.

    Use `||q||^2 - 2 q.x + ||x||^2` (matmul, no Python loop over pairs and no
    `(m, n, d)` broadcast tensor). Floating-point cancellation can produce tiny
    negatives: clamp those to exactly 0, and change nothing else (no abs, no epsilon,
    no rounding of small positive distances).
    """
    raise NotImplementedError("TODO: implement NP-06")


def pairwise_knn(
    queries: np.ndarray,
    candidates: np.ndarray,
    k: int,
    chunk_size: int | None = None,
) -> tuple[np.ndarray, np.ndarray]:
    """Exact k nearest candidates per query by squared Euclidean distance.

    Canonical prompt: given query matrix `Q(m,d)` and reference matrix `X(n,d)`,
    compute pairwise squared Euclidean distances without a Python loop over pairs,
    return exact top-k nearest indices, and support chunked queries when `m*n` scores
    do not fit memory.

    Contract:
    - Rows are sorted by ascending distance; equal distances are ordered by ascending
      candidate index (including ties at the k-th boundary).
    - `chunk_size=None` processes all queries at once; a positive `chunk_size`
      processes at most `chunk_size` query rows at a time, so the distance block is
      `(chunk_size, n)` and peak memory is O(chunk_size * n), not O(m * n). Results
      must not depend on `chunk_size`. A loop over chunks is fine.

    Args:
        queries: `(m, d)`. candidates: `(n, d)`. k: `1 <= k <= n`.
        chunk_size: `None` or a positive int.

    Returns:
        `(distances, indices)`: float64 `(m, k)` squared distances and integer `(m, k)`.

    Raises:
        ValueError: on non-2-D inputs, mismatched `d`, `k` outside `[1, n]`
            (`k > n` is an error, not silently clamped), or non-positive `chunk_size`.
    """
    raise NotImplementedError("TODO: implement NP-06")

import os
import sys
import tracemalloc

import numpy as np

from solution import pairwise_knn, pairwise_sq_distances


def _line_events(fn, *args, **kwargs):
    """Count Python line events executed inside solution.py (timing-free loop detector)."""
    count = 0

    def local(frame, event, arg):
        nonlocal count
        if event == "line":
            count += 1
        return local

    def global_trace(frame, event, arg):
        return local if os.path.basename(frame.f_code.co_filename) == "solution.py" else None

    previous = sys.gettrace()
    sys.settrace(global_trace)
    try:
        result = fn(*args, **kwargs)
    finally:
        sys.settrace(previous)
    return result, count


def _raises(exc, fn, *args, **kwargs):
    try:
        fn(*args, **kwargs)
    except exc:
        return True
    return False


def _double_loop(q, x, k):
    """Required mastery reference: explicit double loop, sort by (distance, index)."""
    dist = np.array([[float(np.sum((qi - xj) ** 2)) for xj in x] for qi in q])
    idx = np.array([sorted(range(len(x)), key=lambda j: (row[j], j))[:k] for row in dist])
    return dist, np.take_along_axis(dist, idx, axis=1), idx

def _line_events(fn, *args, **kwargs):
    """Count Python line events executed inside solution.py (timing-free loop detector)."""
    count = 0

        if event == "line":

        return local

    previous = sys.gettrace()
    sys.settrace(global_trace)
    try:

            order). Orders whose status is 'cancelled' (any case/whitespace) do not count;
            a missing amount counts as 0.0.

def reshape_and_reconcile(frame: pd.DataFrame, dimension: pd.DataFrame) -> tuple[pd.DataFrame, dict]:

class Tracked:
    """Iterator that records pulls and fails fast if consumed far beyond what is needed."""

    def __init__(self, iterable, limit=10_000):
        self._it = iter(iterable)
        self.pulled = 0
        self.limit = limit

    def __iter__(self):
        return self

    def __next__(self):

        value = next(self._it)

import threading
from dataclasses import dataclass
from typing import Any, Callable


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class TaskResult:
    """Outcome of one task: `value` on success, the raised exception in `error` on failure."""

    task_id: int
    ok: bool
    value: Any = None
    error: BaseException | None = None


class WorkerPool:
    """Fixed set of worker threads consuming tasks from a bounded queue.

    Lifecycle: `WorkerPool(...)` -> `start()` -> any number of `submit(...)` ->
    `shutdown()` -> `results()`.

    Contract:
        * `submit` blocks while `max_queue` tasks are waiting (bounded in-flight work).
        * A task that raises is recorded as a failure; the worker keeps processing.
        * `shutdown` stops accepting tasks, lets workers finish every task already
          submitted, then joins all worker threads. Calling it again is a no-op.
        * After `shutdown`, every submitted task has exactly one `TaskResult`; no task is
          lost silently.
        * Must be safe when `submit` is called from several threads at once.
        * No arbitrary sleeps: coordinate with queues/locks/events.
    """

    def __init__(self, workers: int, max_queue: int) -> None:
        """Configure the pool.

        Raises:
            ValueError: If `workers < 1` or `max_queue < 1`.
        """
        raise NotImplementedError("TODO: implement PY-04")

    def start(self) -> None:
        """Start the worker threads.

        Raises:
            RuntimeError: If the pool was already started.
        """
        raise NotImplementedError("TODO: implement PY-04")

    def submit(self, fn: Callable[..., Any], *args: Any, **kwargs: Any) -> int:
        """Enqueue `fn(*args, **kwargs)` and return its task id (0, 1, 2, ... in submit order).

        Raises:
            RuntimeError: If the pool is not started or is shutting down / shut down.
        """
        raise NotImplementedError("TODO: implement PY-04")

    def shutdown(self) -> None:
        """Drain submitted tasks, stop and join the workers."""
        raise NotImplementedError("TODO: implement PY-04")

    def results(self) -> list[TaskResult]:
        """Return results of completed tasks sorted by `task_id`."""
        raise NotImplementedError("TODO: implement PY-04")

import threading

from solution import TaskResult, WorkerPool

TIMEOUT = 5.0


def _raises(exc_type, fn):
    try:
        fn()
    except exc_type:
        return True
    return False


def _run_in_thread(fn):
    """Run fn in a daemon thread; return (thread, done_event, box) so callers can wait."""
    done, box = threading.Event(), {}

    def target():
        try:
            box["value"] = fn()
        except BaseException as exc:  # surfaced to the test via box
            box["error"] = exc
        finally:
            done.set()

    thread = threading.Thread(target=target, daemon=True)
    thread.start()
    return thread, done, box


def _shutdown(pool):
    """Shut down with a deadline so a deadlocked pool fails instead of hanging the suite."""
    _, finished, box = _run_in_thread(pool.shutdown)
    assert finished.wait(TIMEOUT), "shutdown did not finish (deadlock or lost worker?)"
    if "error" in box:
        raise box["error"]

    def blocked():
        started.set()
        assert gate.wait(TIMEOUT)
        return "done"

    pool.submit(blocked)  # taken by the only worker
    assert started.wait(TIMEOUT)
    pool.submit(lambda: 1)  # fills the queue
    _, submitted, box = _run_in_thread(lambda: pool.submit(lambda: 2))
    assert not submitted.wait(0.2), "submit must block while the queue is full"
    gate.set()
    assert submitted.wait(TIMEOUT) and box.get("value") == 2
    _shutdown(pool)
    assert [r.value for r in pool.results()] == ["done", 1, 2]


def test_shutdown_drains_queued_tasks_and_joins_threads():
    baseline = threading.active_count()
    gate = threading.Event()
    pool = WorkerPool(workers=2, max_queue=10)
    pool.start()
    assert threading.active_count() == baseline + 2
    for i in range(8):
        pool.submit(lambda i=i: gate.wait(TIMEOUT) and i)
    shutdown_thread, finished, _ = _run_in_thread(pool.shutdown)
    assert not finished.wait(0.2), "shutdown must wait for submitted tasks"
    gate.set()
    assert finished.wait(TIMEOUT)
    shutdown_thread.join(TIMEOUT)
    assert [r.value for r in pool.results()] == list(range(8))
    assert threading.active_count() == baseline, "worker threads must be joined"


def test_shutdown_while_a_submit_is_blocked_keeps_the_task():
    gate, started = threading.Event(), threading.Event()
    pool = WorkerPool(workers=1, max_queue=1)
    pool.start()

    def blocked():
        started.set()
        return gate.wait(TIMEOUT)

    pool.submit(blocked)
    assert started.wait(TIMEOUT)
    pool.submit(lambda: "queued")
    _, submitted, box = _run_in_thread(lambda: pool.submit(lambda: "late"))
    assert not submitted.wait(0.2)
    _, finished, _ = _run_in_thread(pool.shutdown)
    gate.set()
    assert submitted.wait(TIMEOUT) and finished.wait(TIMEOUT), "shutdown and submit must not deadlock"
    assert box.get("value") == 2
    assert [r.value for r in pool.results()] == [True, "queued", "late"]


def test_lifecycle_errors():
    assert _raises(ValueError, lambda: WorkerPool(workers=0, max_queue=1))
    assert _raises(ValueError, lambda: WorkerPool(workers=1, max_queue=0))
    pool = WorkerPool(workers=1, max_queue=1)
    assert _raises(RuntimeError, lambda: pool.submit(print))
    pool.start()
    assert _raises(RuntimeError, pool.start)
    _shutdown(pool)
    _shutdown(pool)  # idempotent
    assert _raises(RuntimeError, lambda: pool.submit(print))


def test_shutdown_with_no_tasks():
    pool = WorkerPool(workers=3, max_queue=1)
    pool.start()
    _shutdown(pool)
    assert pool.results() == []

import numpy as np

# Canonical prompt: implement entropy and Gini impurity from either class labels or
# class probabilities. Then compute weighted child impurity and information gain for a
# proposed binary split.
#
# Shared contract:
# - Pass exactly one of `labels` (1-D class labels of any hashable kind: ints,
#   negative ints, strings) or `probs` (1-D non-negative, summing to 1 within 1e-9).
#   Anything else raises ValueError, as do empty labels.
# - Optional `weights` (only with `labels`): non-negative per-sample weights with a
#   positive total; class probabilities become weighted class shares. A weight of 2
#   must behave exactly like duplicating the sample.
# - `0 * log(0) = 0`: zero-probability classes contribute nothing (never NaN).
# - Entropy uses log base `base` (2 -> bits, `np.e` -> nats).


def entropy(
    labels: np.ndarray | None = None,
    probs: np.ndarray | None = None,
    weights: np.ndarray | None = None,
    base: float = 2.0,
) -> float:
    """`H = -sum_k p_k log_base(p_k)`."""
    raise NotImplementedError("TODO: implement ML-10")


def gini(
    labels: np.ndarray | None = None,
    probs: np.ndarray | None = None,
    weights: np.ndarray | None = None,
) -> float:
    """`G = 1 - sum_k p_k^2`."""
    raise NotImplementedError("TODO: implement ML-10")

    labels: np.ndarray,
    left_mask: np.ndarray,
    criterion: str = "entropy",
    weights: np.ndarray | None = None,
    base: float = 2.0,
) -> float:
    """`(W_L / W) * I(left) + (W_R / W) * I(right)` for a binary split.

    `W_L`, `W_R` are the children's total sample weights (row counts when `weights`
    is None) and `I` is `"entropy"` or `"gini"`.

    Raises:
        ValueError: if a child is empty (no rows or zero total weight), the mask is
            not boolean with the same length as `labels`, or the criterion is unknown.
    """
    raise NotImplementedError("TODO: implement ML-10")

    labels: np.ndarray,
    left_mask: np.ndarray,
    criterion: str = "entropy",
    weights: np.ndarray | None = None,
    base: float = 2.0,
) -> float:

def best_split(
    x: np.ndarray,
    y: np.ndarray,
    task: str = "classification",
    criterion: str = "gini",
    min_samples_leaf: int = 1,
    sample_weight: np.ndarray | None = None,
) -> dict[str, object] | None:
    """Best depth-1 split `(feature, threshold)` by impurity decrease.

    Canonical prompt: given dense numeric `X(n,d)` and classification labels, find the
    best `(feature, threshold)` split for a depth-1 tree using information gain or
    Gini decrease. Return child predictions. Then adapt the scorer for regression MSE
    reduction.

    Contract:
    - Candidate thresholds for a feature are midpoints `(v_i + v_{i+1}) / 2` between
      consecutive DISTINCT sorted values, so a threshold never separates equal values.
      Rows with `x[:, f] <= threshold` go left.
    - Impurity: classification `criterion="gini"` (1 - sum p^2) or `"entropy"` (base 2);
      regression uses MSE, the weighted mean squared deviation from the weighted mean.
      `gain = I(parent) - (W_L / W) I(left) - (W_R / W) I(right)` with `W` = total sample
      weight (row counts when `sample_weight` is None).
    - Each child needs at least `min_samples_leaf` ROWS.
    - Pick the largest gain; gains within 1e-12 tie and are broken by smaller feature
      index, then smaller threshold. Return None if there is no candidate that
      satisfies the constraints or the best gain is <= 1e-12 (e.g. pure labels or
      constant features).
    - Leaf predictions: classification -> class with the largest (weighted) count,
      ties -> smallest label; regression -> (weighted) mean.

    Returns:
        None, or `{"feature": int, "threshold": float, "gain": float,
        "left_prediction": ..., "right_prediction": ...}`.

    Raises:
        ValueError: unknown task/criterion, non-2-D `x`, length mismatch, NaN in `x`,
            negative weights, or `min_samples_leaf < 1`.

    Complexity: start from a clear O(d * n^2) baseline if you like; the reference sorts
    each feature once and sweeps cumulative statistics for O(d * n log n).
    """

import math

import numpy as np

from solution import best_split


def _raises(exc, fn, *args, **kwargs):
    try:
        fn(*args, **kwargs)
    except exc:
        return True
    return False


def _impurity(y, w, task, criterion):
    if task == "regression":
        mean = np.sum(w * y) / w.sum()
        return np.sum(w * (y - mean) ** 2) / w.sum()
    classes = np.unique(y)
    p = np.array([w[y == c].sum() for c in classes]) / w.sum()
    p = p[p > 0]
    return 1 - np.sum(p * p) if criterion == "gini" else -np.sum(p * np.log2(p))


def _brute(x, y, task="classification", criterion="gini", min_leaf=1, w=None):
    """Naive reference: rescore every midpoint partition from scratch."""
    w = np.ones(len(y)) if w is None else w
    parent = _impurity(y, w, task, criterion)
    best = None
    for f in range(x.shape[1]):
        values = np.unique(x[:, f])
        for t in (values[:-1] + values[1:]) / 2:
            left = x[:, f] <= t
            if left.sum() < min_leaf or (~left).sum() < min_leaf:
                continue
            child = (w[left].sum() * _impurity(y[left], w[left], task, criterion)
                     + w[~left].sum() * _impurity(y[~left], w[~left], task, criterion)) / w.sum()
            gain = parent - child
            if best is None or gain > best[0] + 1e-12:
                best = (gain, f, t)
    return None if best is None or best[0] <= 1e-12 else best

# Canonical prompt: implement linear regression with intercept using gradient descent,
# then add ridge regularization. Separately compute a closed-form reference with a
# numerically appropriate solver rather than explicit matrix inversion. Compare
# predictions/coefficients on a small well-conditioned fixture.
#
# Objective shared by every function (x: (n, d), y: (n,), w: (d,), b: float):

def _line_events(fn, *args, **kwargs):
    """Count Python line events executed inside solution.py (timing-free loop detector)."""
    count = 0

    def local(frame, event, arg):
        nonlocal count
        if event == "line":
            count += 1
        return local

    def global_trace(frame, event, arg):
        return local if os.path.basename(frame.f_code.co_filename) == "solution.py" else None

    previous = sys.gettrace()
    sys.settrace(global_trace)
    try:

    c = np.asarray(components)
    return c.T @ c

    xc = x - x.mean(axis=0)

    order = np.argsort(lam)[::-1]
    return lam[order], vec[:, order].T

def _ref_adam(p, grads, lr, b1, b2, eps, wd, decoupled):
    """Independent multi-step reference written from the equations."""
    m = np.zeros_like(p)
    v = np.zeros_like(p)
    for t, g in enumerate(grads, start=1):
        g_eff = g if decoupled else g + wd * p
        m = b1 * m + (1 - b1) * g_eff
        v = b2 * v + (1 - b2) * g_eff ** 2
        step = lr * (m / (1 - b1 ** t)) / (np.sqrt(v / (1 - b2 ** t)) + eps)
        p = p - lr * wd * p - step if decoupled else p - step
    return p, m, v

# Canonical prompt: implement forward and backward passes for a tiny two-layer NumPy
# network and verify selected analytic gradients with centered finite differences.
# Include a stable loss.
#
# Network (B examples, D inputs, H hidden units, C classes):
#   z1 = x @ W1 + b1        x: (B, D), W1: (D, H), b1: (H,)
#   h  = tanh(z1)           (smooth, so finite differences are well behaved)
#   logits = h @ W2 + b2    W2: (H, C), b2: (C,)
#   loss = mean_i [logsumexp(logits_i) - logits_i[y_i]]     (stable cross-entropy)
# Params are a dict with keys "W1", "b1", "W2", "b2".


def init_params(d_in: int, d_hidden: int, n_classes: int, seed: int = 0) -> dict[str, np.ndarray]:
    """Weights ~ N(0, 1 / fan_in) from `np.random.default_rng(seed)` (W1 drawn before W2);
    biases zero. Same seed -> identical params."""

def forward_backward(
    params: dict[str, np.ndarray], x: np.ndarray, y: np.ndarray
) -> tuple[float, dict[str, np.ndarray]]:
    """Return `(loss, grads)` where `grads[k]` has the shape of `params[k]`.

    Cache the forward intermediates and apply the chain rule (no numerical shortcuts).
    The loss must stay finite for logits around +/-1e4.

    Raises:
        ValueError: on shape mismatches or labels outside `[0, C)`.
    """
    raise NotImplementedError("TODO: implement ML-17")


def numerical_gradient(f: Callable[[], float], array: np.ndarray, eps: float = 1e-5) -> np.ndarray:
    """Centered finite differences of `f()` with respect to every entry of `array`.

    `f` takes no arguments and reads `array`, so perturb entries in place one at a
    time: `(f(a + eps) - f(a - eps)) / (2 * eps)`. Restore each entry afterwards so
    `array` ends bit-for-bit identical. Works for arrays of any shape.
    """

def relative_error(analytic: np.ndarray, numeric: np.ndarray) -> float:
    """`max_i |a_i - n_i| / max(|a_i| + |n_i|, 1e-8)` (0.0 when both are zero)."""
    raise NotImplementedError("TODO: implement ML-17")


def gradient_check(
    loss_and_grads: Callable[[dict[str, np.ndarray]], tuple[float, dict[str, np.ndarray]]],
    params: dict[str, np.ndarray],
    eps: float = 1e-5,
) -> dict[str, float]:
    """For every parameter name, the relative error between the analytic gradient from
    `loss_and_grads(params)` and `numerical_gradient` of its loss. `params` must be
    unchanged afterwards. A correct implementation scores < 1e-6 on smooth fixtures;
    a sign error or a missing chain-rule factor must score far higher."""

import math

import numpy as np

from solution import forward_backward, gradient_check, init_params, numerical_gradient, relative_error


def _raises(exc, fn, *args, **kwargs):
    try:
        fn(*args, **kwargs)
    except exc:
        return True
    return False


def _fixture(seed=0, b=5, d=3, h=4, c=3):
    rng = np.random.default_rng(seed)
    params = {
        "W1": rng.normal(size=(d, h)) * 0.7,
        "b1": rng.normal(size=h) * 0.1,
        "W2": rng.normal(size=(h, c)) * 0.7,
        "b2": rng.normal(size=c) * 0.1,
    }
    return params, rng.normal(size=(b, d)), rng.integers(0, c, size=b)


def _reference(params, x, y):
    """Independent forward/backward written from the equations."""
    z1 = x @ params["W1"] + params["b1"]
    h = np.tanh(z1)
    logits = h @ params["W2"] + params["b2"]
    m = logits.max(axis=1, keepdims=True)
    logp = logits - m - np.log(np.exp(logits - m).sum(axis=1, keepdims=True))
    b = len(y)
    loss = -logp[np.arange(b), y].mean()
    dlogits = np.exp(logp)
    dlogits[np.arange(b), y] -= 1
    dlogits /= b
    dh = dlogits @ params["W2"].T
    dz1 = dh * (1 - h ** 2)
    return loss, {"W1": x.T @ dz1, "b1": dz1.sum(0), "W2": h.T @ dlogits, "b2": dlogits.sum(0)}


def test_implementation_replaces_todo():
    import inspect
    import solution
    for name in ("init_params", "forward_backward", "numerical_gradient", "relative_error", "gradient_check"):
        source = inspect.getsource(getattr(solution, name))
        assert "NotImplementedError" not in source and "TODO: implement" not in source, name


def test_init_params_shapes_scale_and_determinism():
    p = init_params(30, 20, 4, seed=3)
    assert {k: v.shape for k, v in p.items()} == {"W1": (30, 20), "b1": (20,), "W2": (20, 4), "b2": (4,)}
    assert np.all(p["b1"] == 0) and np.all(p["b2"] == 0)
    q = init_params(30, 20, 4, seed=3)
    assert all(np.array_equal(p[k], q[k]) for k in p)
    rng = np.random.default_rng(3)
    assert np.allclose(p["W1"], rng.normal(size=(30, 20)) / math.sqrt(30))
    assert np.allclose(p["W2"], rng.normal(size=(20, 4)) / math.sqrt(20))


def test_forward_backward_shapes_and_values_match_reference():
    params, x, y = _fixture()
    loss, grads = forward_backward(params, x, y)
    ref_loss, ref_grads = _reference(params, x, y)
    assert isinstance(loss, float) and math.isclose(loss, ref_loss, rel_tol=1e-12)
    assert set(grads) == {"W1", "b1", "W2", "b2"}
    for k in grads:
        assert grads[k].shape == params[k].shape, k
        assert np.allclose(grads[k], ref_grads[k], rtol=1e-10, atol=1e-12), k


def test_hand_computed_zero_hidden_case():
    params = {"W1": np.zeros((1, 2)), "b1": np.zeros(2), "W2": np.array([[5.0, -5.0], [1.0, 2.0]]), "b2": np.array([1.0, 0.0])}
    loss, grads = forward_backward(params, np.array([[3.0]]), np.array([1]))
    p = np.exp([1.0, 0.0]) / np.exp([1.0, 0.0]).sum()
    assert math.isclose(loss, -math.log(p[1]))
    assert np.allclose(grads["b2"], p - [0.0, 1.0]) and np.allclose(grads["W2"], 0.0)
    dh = (p - [0.0, 1.0]) @ params["W2"].T  # tanh'(0) = 1
    assert np.allclose(grads["b1"], dh) and np.allclose(grads["W1"], 3.0 * dh[None, :])


def test_batch_gradient_is_mean_of_per_example_gradients():
    params, x, y = _fixture(1, b=6)
    loss, grads = forward_backward(params, x, y)
    singles = [forward_backward(params, x[i:i + 1], y[i:i + 1]) for i in range(6)]
    assert math.isclose(loss, np.mean([s[0] for s in singles]), rel_tol=1e-12)
    for k in grads:
        assert np.allclose(grads[k], np.mean([s[1][k] for s in singles], axis=0))


def test_stable_loss_with_huge_logits():
    params, x, y = _fixture(2)
    params["W2"] = params["W2"] * 1e4
    with np.errstate(over="raise", invalid="raise"):
        loss, grads = forward_backward(params, x, y)
    ref_loss, _ = _reference(params, x, y)
    assert math.isfinite(loss) and math.isclose(loss, ref_loss, rel_tol=1e-9)
    assert all(np.all(np.isfinite(g)) for g in grads.values())


def test_numerical_gradient_is_centered_and_restores_array():
    w = np.array([[0.5, -1.2, 2.0], [1.5, 0.3, -0.7]])
    before = w.copy()
    num = numerical_gradient(lambda: float(np.sum(w ** 3)), w, eps=1e-4)
    assert num.shape == w.shape
    # Centered error is O(eps^2) ~ 1e-8 here; a forward difference is off by ~3*w*eps ~ 1e-4.
    assert np.allclose(num, 3 * before ** 2, rtol=1e-7, atol=1e-9)
    assert np.array_equal(w, before)


def test_relative_error_definition():
    assert relative_error(np.array([1.0, 2.0]), np.array([1.0, 2.0])) == 0.0
    assert math.isclose(relative_error(np.array([1.0, 0.0]), np.array([3.0, 0.0])), 0.5)
    assert math.isclose(relative_error(np.array([1e-9]), np.array([0.0])), 1e-9 / 1e-8)
    assert relative_error(np.zeros(3), np.zeros(3)) == 0.0
    assert math.isclose(relative_error(np.array([1.0, -1.0]), np.array([1.0, 1.0])), 1.0)


def test_gradient_check_passes_correct_backprop_and_leaves_params_intact():
    params, x, y = _fixture(3)
    snapshot = {k: v.copy() for k, v in params.items()}
    errors = gradient_check(lambda p: forward_backward(p, x, y), params)
    assert set(errors) == {"W1", "b1", "W2", "b2"}
    assert max(errors.values()) < 1e-6, errors
    assert all(np.array_equal(params[k], snapshot[k]) for k in params)


def test_gradient_check_flags_sign_error_missing_chain_rule_and_wrong_reduction():
    params, x, y = _fixture(4)

    def sign_error(p):
        loss, g = _reference(p, x, y)
        return loss, {**g, "W2": -g["W2"]}

    def missing_tanh_derivative(p):
        loss, g = _reference(p, x, y)
        h = np.tanh(x @ p["W1"] + p["b1"])
        logits = h @ p["W2"] + p["b2"]
        probs = np.exp(logits - logits.max(1, keepdims=True))
        probs /= probs.sum(1, keepdims=True)
        probs[np.arange(len(y)), y] -= 1
        dz1 = (probs / len(y)) @ p["W2"].T  # forgot * (1 - h**2)
        return loss, {**g, "W1": x.T @ dz1, "b1": dz1.sum(0)}

    def sum_not_mean(p):
        loss, g = _reference(p, x, y)
        return loss, {k: v * len(y) for k, v in g.items()}

    assert gradient_check(sign_error, params)["W2"] > 0.5
    errors = gradient_check(missing_tanh_derivative, params)
    assert errors["W1"] > 1e-2 and errors["b1"] > 1e-2 and errors["W2"] < 1e-6
    assert min(gradient_check(sum_not_mean, params).values()) > 0.3


def test_validation():
    params, x, y = _fixture(5)
    assert _raises(ValueError, forward_backward, params, x[:, :2], y)
    assert _raises(ValueError, forward_backward, params, x, np.array([0, 1, 2, 3, 0]))
    assert _raises(ValueError, forward_backward, params, x, y[:3])

sources.markdown:
# 2026 Generalist MLE Coding Set — FINAL

**Status:** ACTIVE 2026 GENERALIST CODING SET  
**Roadmap window:** Sunday, September 6, 2026 through Thursday, December 31, 2026  
**Count:** 100 coding IDs = 69 roadmap-core + 31 generalist-depth extension IDs  
**Scope:** Deep Generalist MLE interview readiness across SWE/DSA, SQL/data work, Python/NumPy/pandas, classical ML implementation, PyTorch/framework coding, debugging/testing, and production-shaped implementation. Search/IR + Recommendation/Ranking specialization coding remains deferred to the separate specialization curriculum.

## Track counts

| Track | Roadmap core | Depth extension | Total |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| DSA / SWE Algorithms | 26 | 6 | 32 |
| SQL | 9 | 4 | 13 |
| Python / NumPy / pandas | 11 | 7 | 18 |
| General ML Implementation | 9 | 8 | 17 |
| PyTorch / Framework | 7 | 4 | 11 |
| Debugging / Testing / Existing Code | 7 | 2 | 9 |
| **Total** | **69** | **31** | **100** |

## Mastery contract

- **0 — Unseen**
- **1 — Learned:** serious attempt completed; solution understood after review/hints if needed.
- **2 — Interview-ready:** solved independently under the intended time box with correct explanation.
- **3 — Mastered:** solved cold after spacing with edge cases, testing, follow-ups, and complexity/resource defense.

Mastery requires **recognition → reasoning → implementation → validation → explanation**.

Problem formats:
- **LIVE** — realistic interview-sized unit.
- **EXTENDED_DRILL** — staged broader implementation.
- **CAPSTONE** — project/integration work.

For every ★ problem, where applicable, include:
1. one hand-computed fixture;
2. one boundary/empty/singleton case;
3. one invariant/property test;
4. one adversarial bug-revealing case;
5. deterministic-seed/reproducibility checks when randomness exists.


## Practice workflow — VS Code + pytest

Use this workflow whenever a coding ID is turned into a local practice workspace. The purpose is to preserve learner ownership while making every problem executable, testable, reviewable, and easy to revisit cold.

### Default workspace

Create one directory per coding ID:

```text
problems/<problem_id>/
  README.md
  solution.py
  test_solution.py
  notes.md
```

Adapt filenames only when the problem genuinely requires SQL, multiple modules, data fixtures, or framework-specific structure. Keep one canonical problem directory per ID rather than creating a new directory for every attempt.

### File contract

**`README.md`**
- copy the exact canonical interview prompt from this bank;
- state required function/class signatures, inputs, outputs, constraints, and allowed libraries;
- include clarification questions or assumptions that an interviewer could reasonably expect;
- do **not** include the target solution, giveaway pseudocode, or the name of a hidden algorithmic primitive when the interview prompt itself would not reveal it.

**`solution.py`**
- provide imports, public signatures/interfaces, docstrings where useful, and `TODO` markers only;
- do not prefill the intended algorithm in **INTERVIEW** mode;
- the learner owns the implementation.

**`test_solution.py`**
- use deterministic `pytest` tests;
- include ordinary correctness cases plus specification-derived edge cases;
- for ★ problems, include applicable hand-computed fixtures, boundary cases, invariants/properties, adversarial bug-revealing cases, and deterministic-seed checks;
- tests may encode the specification, but should not reveal the intended implementation strategy;
- use tolerances deliberately for floating-point code (`pytest.approx`, `numpy.testing`, or equivalent);
- test shapes, dtypes, ordering, determinism, mutation/state behavior, and failure contracts when they are part of the problem;
- for randomized algorithms, test statistical or deterministic-seed properties rather than brittle exact samples unless exact samples are part of the contract.

**`notes.md`**
- before coding, record clarification, baseline, invariant/objective, intended complexity, and important edge cases;
- after the attempt, record mistakes, failed assumptions, debugging evidence, and the final reasoning;
- keep concise notes that help a later cold re-attempt; do not turn the notes into a copied solution transcript.

### Session modes

Use one explicit mode per practice session:

- **INTERVIEW — default.** Create scaffold + tests, but reveal no solution or giveaway pseudocode. The learner first explains the approach and implements independently under the intended time box.
- **HINT.** Provide the smallest next hint needed: first a diagnostic question, then an invariant/shape/data-grain clue, then a more concrete direction only if needed. Do not jump directly to the solution.
- **REVIEW/SOLUTION.** Enter only after an independent attempt is complete or the learner explicitly requests it. At this point compare implementations, explain the canonical mechanism, repair bugs, improve tests, and discuss alternatives/trade-offs.

### Standard practice loop

For each problem:

1. **Generate the workspace.** Create `README.md`, learner-owned implementation file(s), `test_solution.py`, and `notes.md` from the canonical ID.
2. **Clarify before coding.** State input/output contracts, assumptions, shapes or row grain, edge cases, and allowed libraries.
3. **Reason aloud.** Give a simple baseline, identify the key invariant/objective/equation, and state expected time/memory cost before implementation.
4. **Implement independently.** Stay inside the intended interview time box when doing a timed attempt. Do not consult the solution during INTERVIEW mode.
5. **Run focused tests.** Start with a small relevant subset, then run the full suite, for example:

   ```bash
   pytest -q
   ```

   or, while localizing one failure:

   ```bash
   pytest -q test_solution.py::test_name
   ```

6. **Debug from evidence.** Read the traceback/assertion, localize the failing contract, form a root-cause hypothesis, make the smallest justified fix, rerun the focused test, then rerun the full suite. Do not patch randomly until tests turn green.
7. **Defend the solution.** Explain correctness, complexity/resources, numerical or data issues, tests, and at least one changed-constraint follow-up.
8. **Review only after ownership.** If needed, switch to REVIEW/SOLUTION and compare against a stronger implementation or alternative approach.
9. **Record the lesson.** Update `notes.md` with the specific mistake or transferable insight rather than copying the full answer.
10. **Cold re-attempt later.** Re-solve after spacing, ideally with changed surface wording, inputs, constraints, or one hidden failure mode. Passing the original tests immediately after review is not mastery.

### Workspace setup checklist

A reusable setup checklist is:

```text
Start from the 2026 Generalist MLE coding-set Markdown file.
Set up problem <ID> in INTERVIEW mode for VS Code.
Create the problem workspace with README.md, solution.py (or the appropriate implementation file), test_solution.py, and notes.md.
Preserve the exact canonical prompt and interfaces.
Create a strong deterministic pytest suite, including applicable edge, adversarial, invariant, and numerical cases.
Do not reveal the solution, giveaway pseudocode, or hidden implementation strategy.
```

For SQL problems, use an appropriate SQL file plus deterministic fixture/expected-result tests. For PyTorch, data, or multi-file problems, adapt the workspace while preserving the same ownership and testing contract.

### Pytest acceptance rule

`pytest` passing is necessary but not sufficient. A problem reaches **Interview-ready** only when the learner can also explain why the implementation is correct, derive or state the relevant ML/math mechanism when applicable, reason about complexity/resources, handle material edge cases, and answer the problem's follow-ups without solution dependence.


## Transfer / surprise-resistance contract

The bank is intentionally finite; no problem list can guarantee that an interview will never contain an unfamiliar task. The target is therefore **transfer**, not memorization. Interview-ready performance requires being able to convert an unfamiliar prompt into a correct implementation by identifying its underlying primitive.

For every coding family, practice the following loop:

1. restate input/output contracts and shape/grain semantics;
2. give a simple correct baseline before optimizing;
3. identify the invariant, objective, or mathematical definition being implemented;
4. implement without relying on a convenience library that hides the tested concept unless the interviewer allows it;
5. test a hand-computed example plus adversarial edge cases;
6. state time, memory, numerical-stability, and data-size limits;
7. handle one changed-constraint follow-up;
8. on later review, solve a variant whose surface wording differs from the original problem.

For **ML-concept → code** prompts specifically, be able to move in both directions:

`definition / equation → scalar reference implementation → vectorized implementation → tests → numerical edge cases → complexity`.

For **dataframe / SQL** prompts, explicitly establish row grain, key uniqueness, join cardinality, timestamp semantics, missing-value policy, and deterministic tie handling before implementation.

For **PyTorch** prompts, explicitly track tensor shapes, devices/dtypes, training/eval state, autograd graph lifetime, masking semantics, and reduction denominators.

For **SWE-leaning MLE** prompts, code production-quality interfaces: deterministic behavior where expected, explicit error handling, sensible state ownership, tests, and resource reasoning.

# First-exposure schedule

## Week 1
- **DSA-01 — Two Sum ★**
- **DSA-02 — Group Anagrams**
- **NP-01 — Shapes, Axes, Broadcasting ★**
- **ML-01 — Cosine Similarity + Retrieval**
- **DBG-01 — Leaking Pipeline ★**

## Week 2
- **DSA-03 — Product Except Self**
- **DSA-05 — Container With Most Water ★**
- **SQL-01 — Aggregation / Conversion**
- **NP-02 — Batched Cosine Similarity + Top-K ★**

## Week 3
- **DSA-06 — Three Sum ★**
- **DSA-07 — Longest Substring Without Repeats ★**
- **ML-02 — Classification Metrics + ROC/PR AUC ★**
- **PD-01 — Feature Construction**

## Week 4
- **DSA-08 — Minimum-Size Subarray Sum**
- **DSA-09 — First and Last Position**
- **SQL-02 — Join Grain and Fan-Out ★**
- **ML-03 — Leakage-Safe Splitting ★**

## Week 5
- **DBG-02 — Misaligned Labels / Duplicate Rows**
- **DSA-10 — Binary Search on the Answer ★**
- **DSA-11 — Valid Parentheses**
- **NP-03 — Vectorized Confusion Matrix**

## Week 6
- **ML-04 — Stable Softmax / Cross-Entropy ★**
- **DSA-12 — Daily Temperatures ★**
- **DSA-13 — Linked-List Cycle**
- **SQL-03 — Latest Record Per Entity**

## Week 7
- **PD-02 — Latest Record + As-Of Join**
- **DSA-14 — Reverse Linked List / Reverse Sublist**
- **DSA-15 — Subsets With Duplicates**
- **PT-01 — nn.Module + Shapes**

## Week 8
- **SQL-04 — Top-N Per Group**
- **DBG-03 — Axis / Broadcasting ★**

**Required mastery tests.** reconstruction improves monotonically with k; transformed covariance is diagonal within tolerance for full-rank fixture.

## ML-15 — Naive Bayes From Scratch
**First exposure:** Depth extension  
**Level:** L2  
**Time box:** 30 min  
**Format:** LIVE  

**Interview prompt.** Implement multinomial Naive Bayes for count features with Laplace smoothing and log-space prediction. Return class log-priors, feature log-probabilities, predicted classes, and optional normalized probabilities.

**Core concepts.** conditional independence; smoothing; log probabilities; sparse-count semantics.

**Complexity / resource target.** O(nnz) training/prediction for sparse representation, O(nd) dense.

**Follow-ups / edge cases.** unseen vocabulary; Bernoulli NB; why normalization is unnecessary for argmax.

## ML-16 — SGD, Momentum, RMSProp, Adam, AdamW Updates ★
**First exposure:** Depth extension  
**Level:** L3  
**Time box:** 35 min  
**Format:** LIVE  

**Interview prompt.** Given parameter arrays and gradients, implement one optimizer step for vanilla SGD, momentum, RMSProp, Adam with bias correction, and AdamW-style decoupled weight decay. Keep optimizer state explicit.

**Core concepts.** optimizer state; exponential moving averages; bias correction; coupled L2 vs decoupled decay.

**Complexity / resource target.** O(number of parameters) time; optimizer-state memory accounting.

**Follow-ups / edge cases.** first-step bias correction; zero gradients; mixed precision state dtype.

**Required mastery tests.** hand-computed scalar first/second step; AdamW differs from adding L2 to Adam gradient.

## ML-17 — Gradient Checking + Tiny Neural Net Backprop ★
**First exposure:** Depth extension  
**Level:** L3  
**Time box:** 45 min  
**Format:** EXTENDED_DRILL  

**Interview prompt.** Implement forward and backward passes for a tiny two-layer NumPy network and verify selected analytic gradients with centered finite differences. Include a stable loss.

**Core concepts.** chain rule; cached intermediates; matrix shapes; finite-difference approximation; relative error.

**Complexity / resource target.** analytic backprop O(forward cost); numerical check is intentionally expensive per checked parameter.

**Follow-ups / edge cases.** nondifferentiable activation points; epsilon selection; batch gradients.

**Required mastery tests.** analytic/numeric relative error below tolerance on deterministic small fixture.

# Track E extension — PyTorch / Framework

## PT-08 — Scaled Dot-Product Attention + Masks ★
**First exposure:** Depth extension  
**Level:** L3  
**Time box:** 35 min  
**Format:** LIVE  

**Interview prompt.** Given `Q, K, V` tensors, implement scaled dot-product attention with padding and causal masks. Support batched multi-head shapes, apply masks before softmax, and return both outputs and attention weights.

**Core concepts.** `QK^T / sqrt(d_k)`; tensor transposes; masking; stable softmax; head/batch dimensions.

**Complexity / resource target.** O(B*H*Tq*Tk*d) compute and O(B*H*Tq*Tk) attention-score memory.

**Follow-ups / edge cases.** all-masked row policy; different query/key lengths; flash-attention conceptual follow-up.

**Required mastery tests.** causal future weights are zero; padding weights are zero; rows sum to one when at least one key is valid.

## PT-09 — CNN Module + Shape / Parameter Accounting
**First exposure:** Depth extension  
**Level:** L2  
**Time box:** 30 min  
**Format:** LIVE  

**Interview prompt.** Implement a compact image classifier using convolution, activation, pooling, adaptive pooling, and a linear head. Annotate output shapes and parameter counts after every learned layer.

**Core concepts.** NCHW; convolution output formula; channels; pooling; flatten/adaptive pooling.

**Complexity / resource target.** reason about convolution FLOPs and activation memory qualitatively/quantitatively.

**Follow-ups / edge cases.** arbitrary image size; BatchNorm train/eval behavior; replace pooling with stride.

## PT-10 — Mixed Precision, Inference Mode, and Batched Inference ★
**First exposure:** Depth extension  
**Level:** L3  
**Time box:** 35 min  
**Format:** EXTENDED_DRILL  

**Interview prompt.** Starting from a correct FP32 training/inference loop, add device-aware autocast and gradient scaling where appropriate, then implement memory-bounded batched inference with `eval()` and inference/no-grad semantics. Collect outputs without retaining graphs.

**Core concepts.** AMP; scaler lifecycle; dtype/device; inference graph suppression; batching; host/device transfer.

**Complexity / resource target.** quantify how batch size changes activation memory/throughput; no accidental O(dataset) GPU retention.

**Follow-ups / edge cases.** CPU fallback; unsupported ops; overflow/underflow; why `eval()` and `no_grad/inference_mode` solve different problems.

**Required mastery tests.** evaluation deterministic with dropout; output equivalence to small FP32 fixture within tolerance; GPU-memory state not accumulated across batches conceptually/test where available.

## PT-11 — Freeze / Unfreeze Transfer Learning + Optimizer Groups
**First exposure:** Depth extension  
**Level:** L2/L3  
**Time box:** 30 min  
**Format:** LIVE  

**Interview prompt.** Given a pretrained backbone and new head, freeze the backbone, train only the head, then unfreeze selected layers with a lower learning rate via optimizer parameter groups. Verify which parameters receive gradients and optimizer updates.

**Core concepts.** `requires_grad`; optimizer parameter ownership; train/eval state; differential learning rates.

**Complexity / resource target.** explain compute/memory savings that freezing does and does not provide.

**Follow-ups / edge cases.** BatchNorm behavior while frozen; rebuilding optimizer after unfreeze; discriminative LR.

# Track F extension — Debugging / Testing / Existing Code

## DBG-08 — Performance Regression / Profiling + Vectorization ★
**First exposure:** Depth extension  
**Level:** L3  
**Time box:** 40 min  
**Format:** EXTENDED_DRILL  

**Interview prompt.** A correct NumPy/pandas feature function became 20x slower after a data-size increase. Profile enough to localize Python loops, repeated merges/sorts, unnecessary copies, and an accidental quadratic membership check. Improve it without changing outputs.

**Core concepts.** measurement before optimization; asymptotics; vectorization; allocation/copy behavior; regression tests.

**Complexity / resource target.** state before/after dominant terms plus peak-memory trade-off.

**Follow-ups / edge cases.** vectorization that increases memory too much; chunking; benchmark noise.

**Required mastery test.** correctness against reference + benchmark fixture demonstrating material speedup without hardcoding a machine-specific absolute time.

## DBG-09 — Training / Serving Parity and Version-Skew Bug ★
**First exposure:** Depth extension  
**Level:** L3  
**Time box:** 40 min  
**Format:** EXTENDED_DRILL  

**Interview prompt.** Offline predictions match expected metrics, but a serving path produces shifted scores. Given training preprocessing, serialized transformer state, model weights, and online feature code, localize one preprocessing mismatch, one stale-version mismatch, and one dtype/device/numerical discrepancy. Add parity tests that catch the first divergence.

**Core concepts.** training/serving skew; artifact/version coupling; deterministic replay; intermediate-value comparison; numerical tolerance.

**Complexity / resource target.** diagnostic; design tests that are cheap enough for CI and richer replay tests for periodic validation.

**Follow-ups / edge cases.** unknown categories; model/index coupling; feature freshness; rollback.

**Required mastery test.** a golden request produces matching intermediate features and final prediction within defined tolerance under both paths.

---

# Mixed assessment rotation — required for surprise resistance

Canonical problems build primitives; interviews often combine them. After reaching Interview-ready on most core IDs, rotate through mixed assessments that do **not** reveal which primitive is being tested.

## Mixed A — SWE-heavy MLE screen
- one unseen LeetCode-medium-style problem in 30–35 minutes;
- production-quality function/class interface;
- tests and complexity;
- one changed-constraint follow-up such as streaming, concurrency, or memory cap.

## Mixed B — SQL + pandas data screen
- 20–25 minutes SQL from raw tables;
- 20–25 minutes pandas from analogous DataFrames;
- explicitly reconcile results and explain grain/join differences.

## Mixed C — ML concept → NumPy
Randomly draw one concept from the 2026 knowledge banks and implement the computable core without sklearn/scipy hiding it. Examples include impurity, loss, distance, calibration, resampling, PCA, gradients, probability updates, or a metric. If the exact concept has no canonical coding ID, use the transfer contract rather than adding a new memorized solution immediately.

## Mixed D — PyTorch repair
Receive a short unfamiliar model/training script containing 3–5 issues across shapes, device/dtype, masking, train/eval, autograd lifetime, optimizer order, or metric aggregation. Diagnose before editing; write a focused regression test for each substantive bug.

## Mixed E — Existing-code extension
Given a tested unfamiliar repository component, add one feature without breaking public interfaces or tests. Require code reading, change localization, backward compatibility, and new specification-derived tests.

## Mixed F — Production-shaped implementation
Implement a bounded component such as a batched predictor, feature transformer, cache, rate limiter, replay evaluator, or checkpointable worker. Include API contracts, deterministic tests, failure behavior, and resource reasoning.

A learner who only recognizes canonical IDs but fails these mixed rotations is **not** yet robust to interview surprise.

# Coding acceptance

## Roadmap-core acceptance
- All original **69 roadmap-core IDs** receive serious first exposure.
- Core IDs preserve their existing identifiers and canonical intent so the 2026 roadmap/master can continue to reference them.
- First exposure alone is insufficient; Interview-ready requires independent timed solves and later cold transfer.

## Deep-generalist acceptance
- Complete the **31 depth-extension IDs** or demonstrate equivalent independent mastery through harder transfer variants.
- At least 80% of ★ items across core + extension must have a later cold variant, not a memorized replay.
- Pass at least two Mixed A, two Mixed B, three Mixed C, two Mixed D, one Mixed E, and one Mixed F assessment without solution disclosure.
- No single lane may remain a persistent red zone: SWE/DSA, SQL, NumPy/pandas, ML implementation, PyTorch, and debugging must each support independent interview performance.

## Boundary of sufficiency
This set is designed to make a broad Generalist MLE candidate difficult to surprise across common coding formats. It cannot guarantee coverage of every company-specific puzzle, obscure library API, competitive-programming trick, distributed-systems implementation, or specialization-specific Search/Recs/LLM problem. The defense against those unknowns is the transfer/surprise-resistance contract and mixed assessments, not infinite syllabus growth.

Search/IR + Recommendation/Ranking specialization coding remains owned by the separate specialization set. Future GenAI/LLM specialization should add its own framework/inference/application coding without bloating this generalist bank.

sources.title: 2026 Generalist MLE — Master Instructions
sources.markdown:
# 2026 Generalist MLE — Master Instructions

**Status:** ACTIVE 2026 GENERALIST PROJECT CONTROL FILE  
**Effective roadmap window:** Sunday, September 6, 2026 through Thursday, December 31, 2026  
**Duration:** 17 weeks  
**Authoritative roadmap:** `03_2026_Generalist_MLE_17_Week_Roadmap_FINAL.md`

---

# 0. Instruction to every new 2026 curriculum chat

Before substantive work:

1. Read this master file.
2. Read `03_2026_Generalist_MLE_17_Week_Roadmap_FINAL.md`.
3. Read the relevant core bank(s):
   - `Bank_01_Linear_Algebra_FINAL.md`
   - `Bank_02_Core_ML_FINAL.md`
   - `Bank_05_Deep_Learning_FINAL.md`
   - `Bank_07_Probability_Inference_FINAL.md`
   - `Bank_08_MLE_Practice_FINAL.md`
   - `Bank_09_System_Design_FINAL.md`
4. For coding, read `01_2026_Generalist_MLE_Coding_Set_FINAL.md`.
5. Preserve 2026 IDs, wording, counts, sequencing, mastery rules, and ownership boundaries unless the user explicitly changes them.
6. Do not use Banks 03, 04, or 06 for scheduled 2026 specialization work. Those topics are deferred to the separate 2027 Staff-depth specialization curriculum.
7. For theory sessions, create a new session-scoped Markdown notes artifact.
8. For coding sessions, scaffold/tests are allowed, but do not prefill the solution unless the learner explicitly switches to REVIEW/SOLUTION mode.
9. `04_2026_Session_Start_Prompt_Templates.md` is operational only and cannot override the master, roadmap, banks, or coding set.

## Responsibility rule

- **Master:** purpose, source governance, mastery, workload, ownership boundaries, final acceptance.
- **Core banks:** question IDs, wording, depth, prerequisites/cross-references, required follow-ups.
- **Coding set:** coding IDs, prompts, levels, formats, tests, follow-ups.
- **Roadmap:** weekly sequencing, P0 milestones, review cadence, and mock gates.
- **Session templates:** convenience only.

---

# 1. 2026 source manifest

The intended 2026 source set contains **10 Markdown files**:

| File | Scope |
|---|---|
| `01_2026_Generalist_MLE_Coding_Set_FINAL.md` | 69 core coding IDs |
| `02_2026_Master_Instructions_GENERALIST_MLE.md` | project control |
| `03_2026_Generalist_MLE_17_Week_Roadmap_FINAL.md` | 17-week sequencing |
| `04_2026_Session_Start_Prompt_Templates.md` | operational starters |
| `Bank_01_Linear_Algebra_FINAL.md` | 20 knowledge conversations |
| `Bank_02_Core_ML_FINAL.md` | 23 knowledge conversations |
| `Bank_05_Deep_Learning_FINAL.md` | 27 knowledge conversations |
| `Bank_07_Probability_Inference_FINAL.md` | 24 knowledge conversations |
| `Bank_08_MLE_Practice_FINAL.md` | 23 knowledge conversations |
| `Bank_09_System_Design_FINAL.md` | 13 knowledge conversations |

**2026 totals:** 130 core knowledge conversations + 69 core coding IDs + P0.

Banks 03/04/06 and all 2027 Staff-depth files are outside the scheduled 2026 curriculum.

---

# 2. Purpose

By December 31, 2026, the learner should be **interview-ready for Generalist Machine Learning Engineer roles**.

The learner should be able to:

- reason about linear algebra, probability/statistics, Core ML, and Deep Learning;
- implement common algorithms/ML components in Python/NumPy/PyTorch;
- write and reason about SQL/data transformations;
- debug ML/data/framework failures;
- reason about testing, reproducibility, serving, monitoring, latency, deployment, and retraining;
- design a general ML system end to end;
- defend a production-shaped ML project;
- communicate trade-offs clearly under interview time pressure.

The 2026 objective is **broad Generalist MLE readiness**, not Search/IR + Recommendation/Ranking specialization depth.

---

# 3. Fixed cadence

- Weeks 1–16: **8 new knowledge conversations/week**.
- Week 17: final **2** knowledge conversations + final validation.
- Week 1: **5** new coding IDs.
- Weeks 2–17: **4** new coding IDs/week.
- Total: **130 knowledge + 69 coding**.

The cadence is a first-exposure schedule. Mastery requires spaced re-attempts.

---

# 4. Knowledge scope

## Bank 01 — Linear Algebra
20 conversations.

## Bank 07 — Probability & Inference
24 conversations.

## Bank 02 — Core ML
23 conversations.

## Bank 05 — Deep Learning & Optimization
27 conversations.

## Bank 08 — ML Engineering Practice
23 conversations.

## Bank 09 — ML System Design
13 conversations.

Total: **130**.

Knowledge sessions own:
- explanation;
- derivation where relevant;
- assumptions;
- comparisons;
- failure modes;
- evaluation;
- production/system implications;
- follow-up defense.

---

# 5. Coding scope

The coding set contains:

- DSA / SWE Algorithms — 26
- SQL — 9
- Python / NumPy / pandas — 11
- General ML Implementation — 9
- PyTorch / Framework — 7
- Debugging / Testing / Existing Code — 7

Total: **69**.

Coding owns:
- problem framing;
- implementation;
- correctness;
- tests;
- debugging;
- complexity/resources;
- interview communication;
- cold re-attempts.

---

# 6. P0 — General MLE Pipeline

P0 is the only required 2026 portfolio project.

It should demonstrate:

- public/synthetic/self-generated data;
- clear ML problem/target;
- point-in-time-safe split and features;
- baseline model;
- stronger model or justified alternative;
- evaluation and calibration/thresholding where relevant;
- error/slice analysis;
- testing/data validation;
- reproducible environment/config;
- training loop/checkpointing where relevant;
- minimal batch-scoring or inference interface;
- monitoring/failure analysis;
- safe rollout/rollback reasoning;
- README/architecture diagram;
- limitations;
- interview defense.

Do not add P1/P2/P3 in 2026. Those belong to 2027.

---

# 7. Mastery contract

## Knowledge

0. Unseen  
1. Learned  
2. Interview-ready  
3. Mastered

**Interview-ready:** independent correct explanation with appropriate assumptions, derivation/trade-offs, and follow-ups.

**Mastered:** survives later cold mixed-context recall and connects to coding/project/system design.

## Coding

0. Unseen  
1. Learned  
2. Interview-ready  
3. Mastered

A coding problem is not Interview-ready merely because tests pass.

Interview-ready generally requires:
- correct clarification/assumptions;
- independent approach selection;
- implementation within appropriate time box;
- meaningful testing;
- complexity/resource reasoning;
- core follow-ups;
- coherent communication.

Mastered additionally requires a later cold attempt.

---

# 8. Review queue

Every week prioritize:

1. failed/Red repairs due;
2. first re-attempts due 1–3 weeks after learning;
3. oldest ★ coding item not mastered;
4. oldest high-depth knowledge item not mastered;
5. random cross-domain core item;
6. mixed mock item if capacity remains.

Do not delete due reviews merely to protect new-exposure counts.

---

# 9. Theory session contract

Every theory chat creates a **new session-scoped Markdown file**.

Use:

**canonical question → cold attempt → dynamic probing → diagnose → visible teaching for substantive gaps → update notes → learner reconstruction only when substantive → required follow-ups → mastery state → spaced re-test**

Do not prefill the final answer before a serious cold attempt unless the learner explicitly switches to direct-study mode.

Minor wording/terminology issues do not require reconstruction.

Suggested note sections:

## Canonical Interview Question
## Mastery Answer
## Required / Important Follow-ups
## Plain-English Explanation
## Reasoning Chain
## Interview Compression
## Mastery Record

Keep notes concise and technically rigorous.

---

# 10. Coding / Codex contract

Default mode: **INTERVIEW**.

- INTERVIEW — no solution disclosure.
- HINT — incremental hint ladder.
- REVIEW/SOLUTION — only after explicit learner switch.

Recommended workspace:

```text
problems/<problem_id>/
  README.md
  solution.py
  test_solution.py
  notes.md
```

Adapt for SQL/PyTorch/data/debugging tasks.

Scaffold:
- exact prompt;
- signatures/interfaces;
- deterministic fixtures/tests;
- TODOs;
- no solution;
- no giveaway pseudocode.

Before coding require:
clarify → assumptions → baseline → correctness → complexity → improved approach/invariant.

When tests fail:
interpret → localize → root-cause hypothesis → smallest fix → focused test → full suite.

For ★ problems include applicable:
- hand-computed fixture;
- boundary case;
- property/invariant;
- adversarial case;
- reproducibility check.

After correctness require:
- complexity/resource defense;
- follow-ups;
- code review;
- mastery state;
- cold re-attempt date.

---

# 11. Workload policy

The fixed first-exposure cadence is non-negotiable unless the user changes it:

- 8 knowledge/week Weeks 1–16;
- 2 knowledge in Week 17;
- 5 coding in Week 1;
- 4 coding/week Weeks 2–17.

If overloaded, reduce:
1. optional reading;
2. note polish;
3. optional follow-ups;
4. nonessential project polish.

Do not reduce:
- scheduled first exposure without explicitly rescheduling it;
- due Red repairs;
- essential cold re-tests;
- P0 acceptance work.

---

# 12. Ownership boundaries

Always distinguish:
- professionally owned;
- professionally observed/adjacent;
- independently implemented/studied.

Never reproduce confidential employer code, data, schemas, metrics, or architecture.

Portfolio/preparation work should use public/synthetic/self-generated material.

---

# 13. Final acceptance — December 31, 2026

Acceptance requires:

- all 130 core knowledge conversations exposed;
- all 69 core coding IDs exposed;
- high-priority knowledge/coding largely mastered;
- remaining later items at least interview-ready with re-tests queued;
- P0 complete and defensible;
- successful mixed generalist MLE mock without specialization support;
- ability to handle coding, SQL/data, ML/statistics/DL, debugging, MLE practice, and general ML system design in one interview loop.

The desired outcome is:

> **Interview-ready Generalist Machine Learning Engineer by end of 2026.**

After this gate, begin the separate 2027 Staff-depth Search/IR + Recommendation/Ranking specialization curriculum.
